original_value: To make up the deficiency of artificial intelligent ant colony algorithm in solving the clustering and path planning of wireless sensor network (WSN) a new random disturbance factor is proposed. A self-regulated random disturbance ant colony algorithm is obtained. An improved ant colony algorithm is proposed by combining the self-regulated random disturbance ant colony algorithm with chaos. After the algorithm improvement is completed, the improved artificial intelligent ant colony algorithm is applied to the cluster head fixed WSN node cluster and the path optimization process of each cluster head communication with the base station. The convergence speed, energy consumption and the survival time of the node cluster head are analyzed. The results show that the improved ant colony algorithm has good stability characteristics in the application and convergence of WSN. It can be seen that the improved ant colony algorithm is feasible in clustering and path planning of WSN.

result.paraphrase: To address the shortcomings of the artificial intelligent ant colony algorithm in wireless sensor network (WSN) clustering and path planning, a new random disturbance factor is introduced to form a self-regulated random disturbance ant colony algorithm. By combining this algorithm with chaos, an improved ant colony algorithm is proposed. Once improved, the artificial intelligent ant colony algorithm is applied to fixed cluster-head WSN node clustering and to optimizing the communication paths between each cluster head and the base station. Convergence speed, energy consumption, and cluster-head survival time are then analyzed. The results indicate that the improved ant colony algorithm exhibits good stability in WSN application and convergence, demonstrating its feasibility for WSN clustering and path planning.
